name: Question 3
problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-10y=-5 \\ 2x-4y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}5 & -10 & -5 \\ 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -10 & -5 \\ 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y=-1 \\ 0x+0y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=4$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=4,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

Question 3

Consider the system of linear equations {5x−10y=−52x−4y=2. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.

a
[xy]=[−2+yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
b
No solution
c
[xy]=[−1+2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
[xy]=[2−yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
e
[xy]=[1−2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

M=[5−10−52−42]

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M=[5−10−52−42]R1:=15R1∼[1−2−12−42]R2:=R2−2R1∼[1−2−1004].

The corresponding system is now

{x−2y=−10x+0y=4.

However, the final equation 0x+0y=4 has no solution. It simplifies to 0=4, which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair x,y that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.
